name: Summit Therapeutics Inc.
moat_justification: Weak and approval-contingent: ivonescimab is a potential first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific with Phase 3 evidence (HARMONi PFS benefit; HARMONi-6 first head-to-head overall-survival superiority over an anti-PD-1 regimen in China) and big-pharma validation (AstraZeneca's reported $2B convertible investment, Daiichi Sankyo and Pfizer collaborations), but Summit does not own the molecule — it is in-licensed from Akeso for the US/Canada/Europe/Japan against up to $4.5B in milestones plus low-double-digit royalties, Akeso keeps China and the rest of the world, there is no approved product, no revenue since 2023, no demonstrated pricing power, and returns are deeply negative (fundamentals.json roic_proxy negative in every year shown, -19% to -592%; gross margin not meaningful with no product revenue). CAP 5.9y.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 56.9%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency GBP converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
one_liner: Pre-revenue single-asset oncology biotech, moat 3/10 contingent on approval — owner's earnings are negative in every period (TTM -$1.09/share on -$458M OCF and $384M SBC) with zero revenue since 2023, so it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at any price on an OE DCF; the $14.63 price is an FDA PDUFA option (Nov 14, 2026) on ivonescimab, not an earnings stream.
moat_for: Potential first-in-class PD-1/VEGF bispecific — HARMONi-6 showed overall-survival superiority over an anti-PD-1 combination regimen in a head-to-head Phase 3
Exclusive ivonescimab rights for the US, Canada, Europe and Japan under the Akeso license; BLA accepted with a November 14, 2026 PDUFA date
Big-pharma validation and funding: AstraZeneca's reported $2B convertible preferred investment (2026) plus Daiichi Sankyo / Pfizer trial collaborations
Broad Phase 3 program beyond the first indication (HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7, colorectal and bladder studies) — multiple shots on the same molecule
moat_against: The asset is licensed, not owned — Akeso retains China/rest-of-world and is owed up to $4.5B in milestones plus low-double-digit royalties on Summit-territory sales
Single-molecule concentration: no approved product, zero revenue in 2023-2024 and none filed for 2025 — an FDA refusal is existential
No pricing power demonstrated and entrenched competition (Merck's Keytruda franchise and other PD-(L)1/VEGF combinations) in NSCLC
Deeply negative returns through the whole history (roic_proxy negative every year in fundamentals.json) — no cycle-tested economics exist to defend
Licensor dependence: supply, China data generation and the molecule's origin all sit with Akeso
